title: Topological space
summary: A topology declares which regions count as open, encoding nearness without requiring numerical distance.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared topology context is fixed.

content.plain: A topology declares which regions count as open, encoding nearness without requiring numerical distance.
content.exact: A topology τ on X contains ∅ and X, is closed under arbitrary unions, and under finite intersections; (X,τ) is a topological space.
content.example: Every metric induces a topology through open balls.
content.caveat: Different topologies on the same set create different continuity and convergence behavior.
